stem: A client with heart failure has been prescribed a low-sodium diet. Which statement by the client shows correct understanding of the diet teaching?

options.A: I will compare Nutrition Facts labels and choose foods with less sodium
options.B: I will add table salt to meals when low-sodium foods taste bland
options.C: I will choose more packaged and prepared foods because they are usually lower in sodium
options.D: I do not need to check food labels if a product does not taste salty

rationale: The American Heart Association recommends reading Nutrition Facts labels and comparing packaged foods to choose options with less sodium. It also notes that much dietary sodium comes from packaged, prepared, and restaurant foods and recommends foods low in sodium and prepared with little or no salt. Therefore A shows correct understanding. B adds sodium, C reverses the usual sodium pattern of many processed foods, and D ignores sodium that may not be obvious from taste alone.
educational_objective: Teach a client following a prescribed low-sodium diet to use Nutrition Facts labels and select lower-sodium foods while limiting added salt and high-sodium packaged foods.
source_document_title: The American Heart Association Diet and Lifestyle Recommendations; How to Reduce Sodium in Your Diet
source_version_date: Diet and Lifestyle Recommendations last reviewed 2026-03-31; sodium-reduction guidance current, accessed 2026-08-17
source_locator: Diet and Lifestyle Recommendations: choose foods low in sodium and prepared with little or no salt; read Nutrition Facts/ingredient lists to choose less sodium. How to Reduce Sodium in Your Diet > shopping guidance: compare labels and choose the lowest sodium per serving; packaged/prepared/restaurant foods are major sodium sources
source_claim_supported: A low-sodium eating pattern is implemented by choosing foods lower in sodium, using little or no added salt, and comparing Nutrition Facts labels, particularly for packaged/prepared foods.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)

correction_summary: Kept the item within the context of an already prescribed low-sodium diet rather than asserting a universal sodium target for all heart-failure clients. Rebuilt the stem as a teaching-understanding item, removed the unsupported claim about fluid retention as the direct teaching rationale, and anchored the correct behavior to current AHA label-reading and sodium-reduction guidance.
audit_findings: A is directly supported by current AHA guidance. B adds sodium, C incorrectly assumes packaged/prepared foods are generally lower in sodium, and D ignores label-based sodium information. The item does not prescribe a numeric daily sodium limit or claim that every heart-failure client requires the same restriction. No second answer, cueing, or unresolved conflict remains.
